 Market Today Indian equities extend winning streak for a fifth session.
 Sensex rises 383 points and Nifty gains 150 points.
 Broader indices outperform with midcap and smallcap gains.

 Indian equity benchmarks extended their winning streak to a fifth consecutive session on November 4, supported by a sustained decline in crude oil prices, renewed foreign fund inflows and strong domestic earnings. However, weak global cues and uncertainty surrounding the US midterm election outcome kept investors cautious.
 At close, the Sensex was up 383.55 points or 0.50 percent at 77,301.40, and the Nifty was up 149.75 points or 0.63 percent at 23,960.60.
 Also Read - India's services activity rises to four-month high of 55.8 in October, cost pressures ease 
 The broader indices ended higher and outperformed the main indices with Nifty midcap index adding 1.3 percent and smallcap index rising 2 percent.
 Biggest Nifty gainers were Bharat Electronics, Titan Company, Adani Enterprises, Jio Financial, Max Healthcare, while losers included TCS, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Coal India and BSE Limited.

 On the sectoral front Information Technology index shed 1.5%, while Media index up 5%, Metal & Realty up 2%, while consumer durables, oil & gas, energy, FMCG, up 1% each.
 Also Read - FII selling slows, domestic money holds the line 
 Among individual stocks, BHEL shares surged 6% on orders from Adani Power worth Rs 20,000-28,000 crore, MCX share price shed 5 percent despite better Q2 earnings, Linde India share price rose 10% post strong results.

 Share price of Sai Silks (Kalamandir) added 8% despite weak results, while shares of GNG Electronics jumped 5.6% on strong September quarter earnings, while share of Sedemac Mechatronics fell 3% despite 17.7 percent profit spike.

 Among other stocks, Global Health (Medanta) share price rose 6 percent after the hospital operator reported a 39.3 percent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit.
 Alembic Pharma shares added 11% as Q2 net profit jumps 81% and Chambal Fertilisers share price added 3 percent even net profit declined, while Awfis Space Solutions , Allcargo Terminals and JNK India added 5-9 post Q2 earnings.
 The Indian rupee extended its winning run on fourth straight session on Wednesday, closing marginally higher at 94.64 against the US dollar on Wednesday, compared with the previous close of 94.74.
 Also Read - Gold price optimism cools among Indians: Should investors change their investment strategy? 
 More than 100 stocks touched 52-week high, including Stocks of Emcure Pharma, Welspun Living, Bosch, Adani Ports, PVR INOX, Marico, Indian Hotels, Anand Rathi, Divis Labs, Zydus Life, among others. Click to View More 
 New Listing 
 Shares of M K Sons Fine Jewels ended largely unchanged after listing at Rs 171.60, a 6 percent premium over the IPO price of Rs 162 per share.
 Outlook for November 5 
 Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research, Kotak Neo 
 The benchmark indices continued their positive momentum. The Nifty ended 150 points higher, while the Sensex was up by 384 points. Among sectors, the Media index outperformed, rallying 5.30 percent, whereas the IT index lost the most, shedding 1.50 percent.
 Technically, after a positive open, the market maintained positive momentum throughout the day. A strong higher-high and higher-low formation on the intraday charts and a bullish candle on the daily charts indicate that the uptrend is likely to continue in the near future.
 We are of the view that the short-term market texture is positive, but due to temporary overbought conditions, we could see range-bound activity at higher levels.
 For day traders, buying on intraday dips and selling on rallies would now be the ideal strategy.
 On the downside, 23800-23750/76700-76500 would act as key support zones, while on the higher side, 24000/77500 and 24200/78000 would be the key resistance areas for the bulls. However, below 23750/76500, the sentiment could change. Below this level, traders may prefer to exit their long trading positions.
 Ajit Mishra, SVP – research, Religare Broking 
 Markets edged higher in a volatile session on Wednesday, extending their ongoing recovery. Both benchmark indices, the Nifty and Sensex, gained around 0.5%, reflecting continued resilience after five consecutive sessions of gains. However, the pace of the recovery remained measured as investors assessed global cues and developments surrounding the US midterm elections.
 On the sectoral front, realty, metal and energy stocks outperformed, while IT stocks remained under pressure, declining nearly 1.5%. Broader markets witnessed stronger participation, with the midcap and smallcap indices advancing around 1.6%–2.08%, indicating healthy market breadth and relatively stronger buying interest beyond the frontline indices.
 On the global front, markets remained mixed as investors assessed the implications of the US midterm election outcome, particularly for AI-related investments, global trade and geopolitical developments. Meanwhile, crude oil prices holding around $103 per barrel provided some relief on the macroeconomic front. Continued foreign investor buying and encouraging domestic earnings also lent support to market sentiment.
 The Nifty may witness some consolidation after five consecutive sessions of gains, particularly as the index approaches a crucial long-term moving-average hurdle, the 200-DEMA. Going ahead, the performance of the banking pack, especially leading private sector banks, will be critical in sustaining the recovery and helping the index build a stronger base and inch towards 24,200 next, followed by the 24,400–24,700 zone, while the 23,200–23,500 range is expected to provide immediate support. Meanwhile, participants should remain selective, prioritise stocks displaying relative strength across sectors and avoid averaging down in loss-making counters that continue to lag the broader recovery.
